clue.text: Ambassador has lie-ins regularly with a woman

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the hyphenated word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diplomat enjoys lazy mornings in bed in the company of a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the formal address for an ambassador; the hyphen in 'lie-ins' is ignored when picking letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena is a female given name, so any bearer of it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Way to pay homage to all political leaders after they retire

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the selected letters run backwards
leaders go in front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A suggestion for honouring every party chief once they step down from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay homage' reads as one phrase, but 'pay' works alone as a verb meaning foot (the bill), and 'homage' starts the run of initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpath is a track for walkers, a kind of way or route from place to place.

clue.text: Group of women that is collecting clothes from Nelson Mandela

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British organisation of women's clubs

indicators.note: clothes are what covers the outside, so only the outer letters are wanted

parts.note: first and last letters of the name
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A women's group gathers donated garments from the late South African president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson Mandela' looks like one name, but the clue splits it: 'Nelson' supplies two letters and 'Mandela' alone is the definition. The Women's Institute surrounds 'that is', and the NN goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, Nelson's second wife, was herself a famous anti-apartheid figure known by the surname Mandela.

clue.text: Charlotte Baden's extraordinary crime novel

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their usual order

parts.note: all fifteen letters, including the possessive S

explanation.surface: Praise for a remarkable mystery story written by someone called Charlotte Baden.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S counts as fodder: all fifteen letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards on the Table is a 1936 Agatha Christie mystery featuring Hercule Poirot, so it is a crime novel.

clue.text: Sack a very rich person disregarding society

indicators.note: to disregard is to leave out of account, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: an informal term for a wealthy person
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Fire some wealthy figure who has no time for polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' reads as a verb meaning dismiss, but it is a noun naming the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneybag is literally a pouch or bag for holding money, so it is a type of sack.

clue.text: Perhaps lackey's son to become ordinary kind of farmer

indicators.note: to become is to turn into something else, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a yes-man is a sycophantic follower, and a lackey is perhaps one
S is the abbreviation for son
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: Could a servant's boy grow up to be a plain, everyday farmer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a lackey is an example of a yes-man. Its S, for son, is replaced by O, for ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a yeoman was a man who owned and worked his own small estate, so a farmer of a particular class.

clue.text: End timeless piano piece by Chopin in silence

indicators.note: the suffix -less means without, so the word both names a letter and asks for it to be dropped

parts.note: to quit is to end or stop
T is the abbreviation for time
Chopin wrote famous études, short study pieces for piano

explanation.surface: Finish a Chopin piano piece on an endless note, and then let the room fall quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' supplies both the letter and the instruction: time abbreviates to T, and the suffix removes it from QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Quietude is a literary noun for a state of calm stillness, so it is a synonym of silence.

clue.text: Woman in charge in Italian city

indicators.note: something put in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Verona is a city in northern Italy
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A woman holds the top job in some Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to the abbreviation IC; the second 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a female given name, so any bearer of it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Frank's happy to start firing a gun

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid
to be up is to be in high spirits

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is eager to start shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid; the 's just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops or guns are said to open up when they begin shooting, so the phrasal verb means start firing.

clue.text: Don't dine outdoors after appearance of unknown growth hormone

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities
to eat in is to have a meal at home rather than out

explanation.surface: Advice to skip eating outside once some mysterious growth hormone shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: The unknown letter is placed first because the eating phrase comes after it. Zeatin is obscure, so the friendly wordplay carries the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeatin is a cytokinin, a plant hormone first isolated from maize, which promotes cell division and so plant growth.

clue.text: Foolish admirer filled with energy to become more romantic

definitions.note: the definition is 'more romantic'; 'to become' only joins

indicators.note: something filled has another thing put inside it
foolish means silly or senseless, so the letters lose their sensible order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A lovesick fan, full of zest, hoping to seem more amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: The added E only needs to join the other letters before they are rearranged, so where it sits does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy describes something idealised or wistful, so the comparative form fits as an equivalent of more romantic.

clue.text: Judge changing a plea's not a hot thing

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: changing something alters it, so the letters take on a new order

parts.note: taken as written
no means not any, not a single one

explanation.surface: A judge says that changing one's plea is not a sensational matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot thing' sounds like a fashionable item or a court sensation, but it means something spicy; the English spelling drops the tilde of jalapeño.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeño is a Mexican chilli pepper, valued for its fiery heat, so it is literally a hot thing.

clue.text: Rubbish place to sleep? I'm not sure

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed, often one of a stacked pair
um is the sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up a bed and dismissing it as terrible, then wavering.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue into a hesitant question, and 'I'm not sure' is a spoken filler sound rather than real doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunkum is informal for nonsense or empty talk, in the same sense that rubbish means foolish talk.

clue.text: Going crazy here, late tonight, fully undressed

indicators.note: going crazy means losing one's sense of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all fifteen letters, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A wild party in full swing late at night, with everyone stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas break the fodder into what looks like a scene-setting phrase, but every letter of 'here late tonight' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: In the altogether is an informal British idiom for being naked, wearing nothing at all.

clue.text: Groups of 9 or 11 out of 12 houses may be labelled thus?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nonary is a set of nine

definitions.text: 11 out of 12 houses may be labelled thus?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split as two words: the twelve houses of the zodiac, of which all but one are not Aries

explanation.surface: A puzzle about numbered groups and houses on a street, as if sorting addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' suggests buildings on a street, but these are the twelve signs or houses of the zodiac; only one is Aries, so the rest could be called non-Aries.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonary comes from Latin for ninefold, and as a noun names a set of nine items; the other reading is a playful compound.

clue.text: Shock when nonsense's written about Northern Ireland

parts.note: as and when both mean at the time that

indicators.note: writing that goes about something wraps around it, so it holds another piece inside

parts.note: tosh is British slang for nonsense
NI is the standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Dismay when rubbish gets printed about the politics of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the nonsense to its instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock and to astonish both mean to surprise someone greatly, so the verbs are synonyms here.

clue.text: Herb Alpert ultimately right to visit part of Spain

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter is used

parts.note: final letter of the surname

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece enters another

parts.note: Aragon is a region of north-east Spain
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The trumpeter Herb Alpert finally gets permission to tour a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb Alpert' reads as the American trumpeter's name, but 'Herb' alone is the definition and 'Alpert' supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic plant whose leaves are used in cooking, especially in French cuisine, so a culinary herb.

clue.text: Think about giving welcome to good man

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word runs backwards
welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Consider extending a warm reception to a virtuous fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good man' looks like the definition, but 'good' gives its letter and 'man' alone is defined, in the chess sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are often called men, and a knight is one of those pieces on the board.

clue.text: Stars laid-back in carefree surroundings

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so one piece sits within another
surroundings enclose whatever is placed among them, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: gay in its older sense means lighthearted and carefree
lax and laid-back both mean relaxed or casual

explanation.surface: Celebrities relaxing in a happy, easygoing setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like famous people, but it means celestial bodies; 'laid-back' is not a reversal signal but a synonym for relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of billions of stars bound by gravity, so the plural noun is a fair definition.

clue.text: Attention diminishes with medication

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention to them
drops and diminishes both mean falls or decreases

explanation.surface: Someone's focus fades once they take their medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drowsiness from pills, but the pieces are a body part and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear drops are a liquid treatment put into the ear to treat infection or wax, a form of medication.

clue.text: Back of computer connected to external device

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word
outer and external both mean on the outside

explanation.surface: A port on the rear of a PC is plugged into some peripheral gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface sounds like tech-support instructions, and the answer belongs in that picture, though only 'device' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a piece of networking hardware that forwards data between computers, so it is a device.

clue.text: Matter of indifference?

parts.note: surface reading: something unimportant, a thing nobody cares about
setter's reading: a bodily substance that is also a word for calm, unemotional coolness

explanation.walkthrough: 'A matter of indifference' is an idiom for something trivial, but here 'matter' is a substance, and the answer also names an unruffled temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm is mucus, a bodily matter, and in old medicine the humour causing a calm, apathetic temperament, hence phlegmatic.

clue.text: State extremists in Syria transfixed by row about Israel's borders

indicators.note: something transfixed is pierced right through, so another piece runs into its middle
extremists are those at the far ends, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of the country

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a rank is a row or line, as of soldiers or taxis

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outer letters are used

parts.note: first and last letters of the country

explanation.surface: Militants in Syria are caught up in a dispute along Israel's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, fitting the Middle East surface, but it means a line. Israel's two outer letters go into it, and the result goes between Syria's.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation in the Indian Ocean, an independent country and therefore a state.

clue.text: Diffuse nebula lacking in strength

indicators.note: diffuse means spread out and scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes that a hazy cloud of gas in space is faint.
explanation.walkthrough: A diffuse nebula is a real astronomical term, so 'Diffuse' passes as a plain adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable means lacking the power or capacity to do something, which matches lacking in strength.

clue.text: Son of Darius succeeded old king from the East

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading from right to left

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
ex means former, as in ex-wife
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A history lesson: a Persian prince took over from an ancient Eastern monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits Persian history, since Xerxes did succeed Darius; but 'succeeded' is just a letter and 'from the East' turns the string around.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes I, king of Persia who invaded Greece in 480 BC, was the son and successor of Darius the Great.

clue.text: In confusion, I googled "keep a low profile"

indicators.note: confusion is disorder, so the letters are muddled into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Baffled, someone searched online for how to stay out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a search query, but the quoted words are the definition and 'I googled' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lie doggo is informal British slang meaning to stay hidden and quiet, avoiding attention, much as an idiom for keep a low profile.
